reports.renderedText: The first time the creature becomes bloodied. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, other creatures in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: No effect.

While the monster has more than half its Hit Points, it gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class. When it first becomes Bloodied, this bonus ends and its walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the encounter.
The monster's speed is 0, it is immune to the Prone condition, and the reach of its melee attacks increases by 5 feet. Forced movement moves it only half the normal distance.

The monster has Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to end the Grappled or Restrained condition. Immediately after it ends either condition, it can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

At the start of combat, define one short directive containing a verb and a subject. While that directive can be obeyed, the monster prioritizes it over every other objective and interprets it literally. If the directive becomes impossible, the monster attacks the nearest creature until a path to the directive reappears.
At the start of its turn, the monster moves up to 10 feet toward its quarry without provoking Opportunity Attacks and must include that quarry among its attack targets if able.

At the start of its turn, the monster chooses a destination it can see. Until the end of the turn, it follows the shortest passable route toward that destination and cannot willingly change destinations. It ignores nonmagical difficult terrain created by rubble, corpses, mud, or loose bones while moving along that route.

The monster moves up to half its speed in a straight line without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If it moves at least 15 feet and then hits with a melee attack before the end of the turn, it pushes the target 5 feet. The monster cannot take reactions until the start of its next turn.

The monster can move through openings as though it were one size smaller and can move through the spaces of prone or dead creatures, treating those spaces as difficult terrain. It is immune to the Prone condition, but it cannot climb or jump farther than 5 feet.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 17 (3d10) Bludgeoning damage. If the creature moved at least 10 feet straight toward the target this turn, the target takes an extra 3 (1d4) Bludgeoning damage.
The monster pins the target against that surface.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Bludgeoning damage and must make a Strength Saving Throw. Strength Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: The target is pushed 5 feet. If it collides with a creature or object, both take the monster's Proficiency Bonus Bludgeoning damage. Success: The target is not pushed.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, one Large or smaller creature within reach. Failure: The target has the Grappled condition and has the Restrained condition while the grapple lasts. The target can escape with an Athletics or Acrobatics check against DC 13. Success: The target is not grappled.

Recharge 5-6. Strength Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Cone originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 8 (3d4) Thunder damage and has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 17 (3d10) Bludgeoning damage. If the creature moved at least 10 feet straight toward the target this turn, the target takes an extra 3 (1d4) Bludgeoning damage.

Recharge 5-6. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 30-foot Cone originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 14 (3d8) Acid damage and is covered in purge fluid. While covered, it can't regain Hit Points and takes the monster's Proficiency Bonus Acid damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can take an action to clean the fluid with a suitable approach. Success: Half damage only.
Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Bludgeoning damage, and the monster pulls it up to 5 feet toward itself.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, one Large or smaller creature within reach. Failure: The target has the Grappled condition and has the Restrained condition while the grapple lasts. The target can escape with an Athletics or Acrobatics check against DC 13. Success: The target is not grappled.
The monster gains 1 Pressure, to a maximum of 3. The number of Pressure markers is visible. At 3 Pressure, it must use Pressure Vent at the start of its next turn.

At the start of the monster's turn while it has 3 Pressure. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, other creatures in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 3 (1d4) Poison and Thunder damage and is pushed 5 feet away from the monster. Success: Half damage only. The monster loses all Pressure. Before the vent, an adjacent creature can use an action to puncture a blister and choose a 15-foot Cone instead.
Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, other creatures in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 3 (1d4) Poison and Slashing damage. Success: Half damage only.

The first time the monster becomes bloodied. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, other creatures in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 13 (5d4) Poison and Thunder damage and has the Prone condition. Success: Half damage only. The monster drops to 0 Hit Points. Before the blast, an adjacent creature can use an action and pass Sleight of Hand or Investigation against the save DC to cancel it; the monster loses Reactions until its next turn.

If damage reduces the monster to 0 Hit Points, unless the damage is Radiant or from a Critical Hit, the monster makes a Constitution Saving Throw with a DC equal to 5 plus the damage taken. On a success, it drops to 1 Hit Point instead.
The monster deals double damage to objects and structures.
The first time each encounter the monster destroys a Large or larger object or section of structure, the resulting 10-foot space becomes difficult terrain and grants Half Cover until cleared.

If the monster has the Prone, Restrained, or Incapacitated condition, a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to make one melee attack against its head. On a hit, the attack becomes a Critical Hit, and the monster can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

At the end of a turn, if the Bloodied monster took at least 8 Slashing damage during that turn, one of its limbs is severed and it gains 1 Exhaustion level. The monster can suffer this effect no more than once per round and regrows its missing limbs and removes all Exhaustion levels gained from this trait the next time it regains Hit Points.

After the monster takes Radiant damage, it can't take Reactions or benefit from a trait that would prevent it from dropping to 0 Hit Points until the start of its next turn. If it drops to 0 Hit Points during that time, its Death features don't activate.

When the monster dies, a 10-foot-radius bloom spreads from its space. The area is Difficult Terrain. A creature that starts its turn in the bloom can't regain Hit Points until the start of its next turn. Fire or Radiant damage dealt to the corpse destroys the bloom. A creature adjacent to the corpse can use an action to clear one 5-foot square.

The monster dies or drops to 0 Hit Points. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, other creatures in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 20 (8d4) Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. Success: The target takes half damage only.

When the monster dies, a 10-foot-radius slick spreads from its space and lasts until cleared. The area is Difficult Terrain. A creature that enters the slick for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Dexterity saving throw, falling Prone on a failed save. A creature can use an action to clear one 5-foot square with fire, sand, cloth, water, or another suitable method.

On initiative count 20, choose a floor point within 60 feet with a corpse, drain, vent, or fluid. A 15-foot-radius Lightly Obscured cloud lasts until the next initiative count 20. A breathing creature starting there makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet and it can't take Reactions until its next turn. Creatures above the floor or that don't breathe are unaffected. Opening a connected exterior passage ends the cloud.
Select the corpses, mark their 5-foot hazard areas, and remove each marker when it bursts, is vented, or is safely destroyed.

At the start of combat, the monster marks one visible creature carrying a holy symbol, funerary object, grave soil, or open wound as its Bearer of Shame. It prioritizes that creature. A different creature can visibly present a funerary offering to become the new Bearer.
Once per encounter, immediately after the monster damages its Bearer of Shame, it regains Hit Points equal to twice its Proficiency Bonus.
The monster moves toward the nearest visible unattended corpse before pursuing other objectives.

The monster consumes part of the corpse and gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice its Proficiency Bonus. Until the start of its next turn, it cannot take Reactions and has disadvantage on attack rolls against living creatures.
While in Bright Light, the monster cannot willingly end its turn farther from Dim Light or Darkness if a safe route toward either exists.
The monster takes the Hide action. While in Dim Light or Darkness, it has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
The monster can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while it is on the Material Plane. It also knows whether an unattended corpse it can see is inhabited, animated, or spiritually anchored.

The monster enters an unattended Medium or larger corpse within 5 feet. While anchored, its speed is 0, it has Half Cover, and it cannot be moved against its will. It can leave the corpse as a Bonus Action. It is expelled into an adjacent space if the corpse is destroyed, burned, or moved more than 10 feet at once.

The monster can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but it cannot end its turn inside an object. The first time each turn it enters a solid object, a visible frost outline appears on the surface nearest its intended exit and remains until it emerges or the turn ends.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Necrotic damage. If the target is below half Hit Points, the monster gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature within 10 feet of a corpse. Failure: The target is pulled adjacent to the corpse and has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn. Success: No effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Necrotic damage. If the target is not Undead, it makes a Constitution Saving Throw. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: At the end of its next Long Rest, the target gains 1 Exhaustion level, to a maximum of 3 levels from this feature. Success: No disease effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Necrotic damage. If the target is below half Hit Points, the monster gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: a target has the Restrained condition for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Success: No effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: 8 (3d4) Piercing damage. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: At the end of its next Long Rest, the target gains 2 Exhaustion levels, to a maximum of 4 levels from this feature. If it fails by 5 or more, it also contracts the disease for 1d4 weeks. Success: No disease effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Necrotic damage. If the target is below half Hit Points, the monster gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: a target has the Restrained condition for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Success: No effect.

Recharge 5-6. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, non-undead creatures that can see the spirit in a 30-foot Cone originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 4 (1d6) Psychic damage and has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: The target takes half damage and is immune to this spirit's Horrific Apparition for 24 hours.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Necrotic damage. If the target is below half Hit Points, the monster gains Temporary Hit Points equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: a target has the Restrained condition for 1 minute. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Success: No effect.
The monster consumes the corpse, ends one condition affecting it, and gains 5 temporary Hit Points.
The monster's speed increases by 10 feet, and it cannot benefit from being Invisible or disguised. This state ends when those temporary Hit Points are gone.

The monster can appear and sound like a mundane person whose corpse it has consumed. A creature can spend an Action testing the disguise with a specific memory, funerary record, or physical evidence, making an Insight or Investigation check contested by the monster's Deception. On a success, the disguise is exposed to every witness who can perceive the evidence.
The monster loses its Reactions and must route toward its Identity Anchor or a usable corpse on its next turn.

The monster has the Invisible condition and moves up to half its speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The Invisible condition ends when this movement ends, if the monster enters bright light, or immediately after it makes an attack roll.

The monster chooses one option: Rush, moving up to half its speed toward a visible enemy; Slip, moving up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; or Stalk, taking the Hide action if it is obscured or behind cover.

The monster is indistinguishable from an ordinary corpse. A creature within 5 feet can use an action to make a Wisdom (Medicine) or Intelligence (Investigation) check against the monster's save DC, identifying it on a success.
The monster can move up to half its speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. A creature that did not identify it cannot take reactions until the start of that creature's next turn.

The monster moves up to its speed toward the witness without provoking Opportunity Attacks. For 1 minute, the first time each turn it hits a visible witness, it deals extra Necrotic damage equal to its Proficiency Bonus, and it cannot willingly end its turn farther from every visible witness. The rage ends early if it starts a turn unable to see a witness.
While in sunlight, the monster has Disadvantage on D20 Tests, and its Speed is halved. Magical light counts as sunlight only if the effect creating it says that it is sunlight.

When the monster starts its turn within 5 feet of a corpse, one witness within 30 feet that can see it can use a Reaction to denounce its hunger or speak its mortal name. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: The monster can't take Reactions, its Speed is halved, and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn. Success: The monster is immune to this witness's Shame for 24 hours.

A creature can spend 1 minute and expend a flask of Holy Water or 10 GP of ritual salt and incense to prepare a corpse as bait. The first time the monster enters a space within 5 feet of that corpse or starts its turn there, it takes 2d6 Radiant damage and has the Restrained condition until the end of its next turn.

A creature within 30 feet of the monster can take a Magic action to present burial salt, perform a funeral invocation, or speak the monster's true name. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: Until the end of its next turn, the monster can't willingly move closer to that creature, enter that creature's space, or move through creatures or objects. Success: The monster is immune to that creature's Salt and True Names for 24 hours.

When the monster dies, spectral dust fills a 10-foot-radius area until the end of the next round. Invisible creatures and objects in the dust are visibly outlined and gain no benefit from being Invisible, and creatures in the dust can't take the Hide action. Strong wind disperses the dust.
A creature uses an action to study the dust and learns either the direction of the monster's last feeding place or the identity of its last victim.

The monster dies or drops to 0 Hit Points. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, the killer, or the nearest creature that can hear it. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn and sees one memory from the monster's last victim. Success: The target sees that memory. A target that used its Reaction to reject it learns nothing.

On initiative count 20, the monster chooses a funerary object or corpse within 60 feet. A 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on it is silent until the next initiative count 20. Creatures entirely inside are Deafened and can't cast spells with Verbal components. Moving the anchor 10 feet, covering it, or dealing Radiant damage to it ends the effect.
A respectful offering can be food, coin, flowers, incense, a grave good, or another culturally appropriate funerary object.
At the start of combat, designate one visible allied creature, egg cluster, webbed object, or occupied nursery space as the Brood. The monster prioritizes enemies within 10 feet of the Brood.
The monster moves up to half its Speed toward the triggering creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

The monster begins combat carrying three visible eggs. Each egg is a Tiny object with AC 10, 1 Hit Point, immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and vulnerability to Fire damage. While any eggs remain, the monster's speed is reduced by 10 feet. The final egg's destruction ends this penalty.
One surviving egg hatches into one spider minion in an adjacent unoccupied space.

The monster has a climb speed equal to its walking speed and can move across difficult surfaces and ceilings without making an ability check. While touching a wall or ceiling, it is immune to the Prone condition while attached. Forced movement that pulls it away from the surface causes it to fall normally.
The monster ignores movement restrictions caused by webs. While touching a web, it knows the location of every other creature touching the same connected web and cannot be surprised by any of them.
The triggering creature takes 3 (1d4) Piercing damage. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.
In Dim Light or Darkness, the monster has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. Bright Light or Fire or Radiant damage suppresses this benefit until the end of its next turn.
The monster has 1 Hit Point. An allied spider within 5 feet can use a Bonus Action to devour it, destroying it and gaining Temporary Hit Points equal to twice that spider's Proficiency Bonus.
The monster cannot be Surprised while conscious and gains a bonus to Passive Perception equal to its Proficiency Bonus.
Until the start of the monster's next turn, the target gains no benefit from being unseen by the monster unless its sight is disabled, every eye is covered, or Line of Sight is denied.
The monster has a climb speed equal to its walking speed and can move across walls and ceilings without making an ability check.
Once on each of its turns after descending at least 10 feet from a wall or ceiling, the monster can move up to 10 additional feet on the ground without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

The monster creates a web line between itself and a surface within 30 feet it can see, then moves along the line up to its remaining speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The line remains as a visible fragile object vulnerable to fire until destroyed.
The monster can move along any intact web line it created as though the line were a climbable surface. It ignores movement restrictions caused by its own web lines.

The monster chooses an unoccupied space in darkness within 20 feet that it can see. The source and destination shadows visibly stretch toward each other, then the monster teleports to the destination. Bright light on either space before the teleport resolves prevents the movement without expending the use.
The monster chooses an unoccupied landing space within 20 feet that it can see, visibly crouches toward it, and jumps there without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Poison damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. The target has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions. The condition lasts 1 hour. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, it has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions for 1 hour. Success: No additional effect.
Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 30/120 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Poison damage.

Recharge 5-6. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed. The web has low AC and Hit Points, vulnerability to Fire damage, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Success: No effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: The wound keeps bleeding. The target takes Piercing damage equal to the monster's Proficiency Bonus at the start of each of its turns until it receives healing or a creature succeeds on a Medicine check to close the wound. Success: No ongoing wound.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Poison damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. The target has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions. The condition lasts 1 hour. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, it has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions for 1 hour. Success: No additional effect.

Recharge 5-6. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed. The web has low AC and Hit Points, vulnerability to Fire damage, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Success: No effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Poison damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. The target has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions. The condition lasts 1 hour. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, it has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions for 1 hour. Success: No additional effect.

Recharge 5-6. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed. The web has low AC and Hit Points, vulnerability to Fire damage, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Success: No effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Poison damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. The target has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions. The condition lasts 1 hour. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, it has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions for 1 hour. Success: No additional effect.
Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 30/120 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Poison damage.

Recharge 5-6. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed. While restrained by the web, the target takes 3 (1d4) Slashing damage at the start of each of its turns. Shadow webs have higher AC and Hit Points than ordinary webs. Success: No effect.
Ranged Attack Roll: +6, range 60/120 ft. Hit: the target takes 11 (2d10) Poison damage, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of the monster's next turn.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Poison damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. The target has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions. The condition lasts 1 hour. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, it has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions for 1 hour. Success: No additional effect.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Piercing and Poison damage and must make a Constitution Saving Throw. The target has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions. The condition lasts 1 hour. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: If this damage reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, it has the Paralyzed and Poisoned conditions for 1 hour. Success: No additional effect.

Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, one target. Failure: The target's speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it takes 3 (1d4) Piercing damage at the start of its next turn. An action and a successful Medicine check ends the effect. Success: No effect.

Recharge 5-6. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition until the web is destroyed. The web has low AC and Hit Points, vulnerability to Fire damage, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Success: No effect.

The monster moves up to half its speed toward the triggering creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Until the end of its next turn, its speed increases by 10 feet and it cannot willingly move farther from that creature.
The monster marks two visible web anchors. Each anchor is a fragile object that can be cut, burned, occupied, or destroyed.

The first time the monster becomes bloodied, each new wall occupies a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide Line between two surviving anchors. The wall is difficult terrain and grants Half Cover through it until an anchor is destroyed or the wall is burned or cut.

The first time each round a web created by the monster is destroyed. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, the affected space in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 3 (1d4) Acid damage. Success: Half damage only. The affected space is difficult terrain until the end of the monster's next turn.

At the start of combat, the monster marks one visible creature that is isolated, Restrained, wounded, or farthest from its allies as its Quarry. It can choose a new Quarry when the current one becomes unreachable or ends its turn adjacent to an ally.
The monster takes the Hide action.

The grounded monster is moved at least 5 feet against its will or enters an unstable surface. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13. Failure: The monster has the Prone condition, and its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn. Success: No effect.

After the monster takes Fire damage, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn. During that time, it can't willingly move closer to the source of the Fire damage.

When the monster jumps, changes between a wall, ceiling, and floor, or gains the Prone condition, its underbelly is exposed until the start of its next turn. Attack rolls against it have Advantage during that time, and the first hit deals an extra 1d6 damage of the attack's type.

When a creature hits the monster with a ranged weapon attack, it can forgo all damage from that attack to strike the eye cluster. The monster has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. After this blindness ends, the monster is immune to Eye Cluster until the start of its following turn.

The monster carries a visible Brood Sac. The sac has AC 12, Hit Points equal to 5 + twice the monster's Proficiency Bonus, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. A creature can target the sac as though it were an object carried by the monster. When the sac is destroyed, the monster can't take Reactions and has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

When the monster dies, up to one intact egg it carries hatches immediately into one spider minion in an adjacent unoccupied space. The minion rolls Initiative. Destroyed eggs and eggs exposed to Fire damage since the end of the monster's previous turn can't hatch.

The monster dies or drops to 0 Hit Points. Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 13, the nearest creature. Failure: The target has the Restrained condition in silk until it escapes or the silk is destroyed. Success: No effect. The silk has AC 10, Hit Points equal to 5 + the monster's Proficiency Bonus, and Vulnerability to Fire damage.
A creature uses an action to cut open the cocoon without damaging its contents, revealing one carried trophy, clue, or sign of a missing victim.
Mark each armed square and remove its marker after its first trigger or when it is disabled.

On initiative count 20, webbing fills a 20-foot Cube within 60 feet. Each creature there without Web Walker makes a Dexterity saving throw, becoming Restrained on a failure. A restrained creature can use an action and pass Athletics against the save DC to escape. Each 5-foot section has AC 10, 5 Hit Points, Fire vulnerability, and Poison and Psychic immunity. Only one Broodmother Web can exist; while it remains, the monster can't use another Lair Effect.
Mark no more than two persistent regions. Creating a third removes the oldest region from play.
The monster has Resistance to Cold and Necrotic damage, but it cannot regain Hit Points. After it takes Fire damage, these resistances are suppressed until the start of its next turn.

A creature first sees the mask clearly. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature. Failure: The target cannot take Reactions against the monster and cannot willingly move closer to it until the start of its next turn. Success: No effect.

Once per round, when no conscious hostile creature has line of sight to it, the monster can move up to half its speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This movement ends immediately if a conscious hostile creature regains line of sight to it.

Choose a mask until removed. Mourner grants +10 Speed and imposes Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against it. Accuser adds its Proficiency Bonus as Psychic damage to its first hit each turn against a Frightened creature. Saint ends one condition and grants Advantage on its next saving throw before the end of its next turn. Fire suppresses the benefit until its next turn. While Grappled or Restrained, an adjacent creature can use an action and pass an Athletics or Sleight of Hand check against the save DC to remove the mask.

After the monster takes Fire damage, the wax remains softened until the start of the monster's next turn. Attack rolls against it have Advantage during that time. The first hit during the window tears the mask, and the monster can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

Melee Attack Roll: +6, reach 5 ft. Hit: the target takes 14 (3d8) Cold and Necrotic damage. If the monster is wearing or presenting a recognizable face, it can move 10 feet after the hit without provoking opportunity attacks from that target.

The monster dies or drops to 0 Hit Points. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, one creature that can see the mask. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition and can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn. Success: No effect. A target that averted its gaze can't see the corpse's space until the start of its next turn. This effect doesn't trigger if the mask was destroyed before the monster died.

A breathing creature other than the monster starts its turn in the aura. Constitution Saving Throw: DC 13, other creatures that can breathe in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Poisoned condition until the start of its next turn. Success: The target is immune to this monster's Stench for 24 hours.

The first time the monster becomes bloodied. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, hostile creatures that can see the monster in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target has the Frightened condition and cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn. Success: A creature can use its reaction to avert its eyes and automatically succeed, but it cannot see the monster until the start of its next turn. Otherwise, no effect.

Recharge 6. Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 13, creatures that can hear the monster in a 20-foot Emanation originating from the creature. Failure: The target takes 4 (1d6) Psychic damage and has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn. Success: The target takes half damage. A creature that cannot hear the monster automatically succeeds.
